solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Union official's split about American aim again

indicators.note: the official's title is said to split the pair of short words, so it goes between them

parts.note: RE is the Latin-derived 'concerning', i.e. about
FOC, Father of the Chapel, is the senior shop steward of a print or newspaper union branch

explanation.surface: A trade unionist splits from colleagues over some American objective.
explanation.walkthrough: FOC (Father of the Chapel) is a British printing-trade union title, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a lens or one's attention onto a target once more is to train it anew on that target.

clue.text: Further address rising row about half-a-dozen sons

indicators.note: the reversed row goes about, around, the numeral and sons
in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
VI is the Roman numeral for six
S is short for son

explanation.surface: A rising row over six sons calls for the matter to be addressed again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns TIER into REIT, which goes round VIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit a subject is to return to it and deal with it once more.

clue.text: Stone found below tree tops

indicators.note: in this down clue the stone abbreviation sits beneath the tree word

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
ST is short for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A stone is found under the treetops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' is a noun-looking word but here a plural noun: the winners, the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Firsts are top-ranked results, the best performers, so the tops.

clue.text: Celebrated completion of fine railway junction

parts.note: crew is the British past tense of crow, to exult or boast

indicators.note: the completion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: People cheered the finishing of a splendid railway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: This town in Cheshire is a famous English railway junction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheshire town grew up around one of Britain's major rail interchanges.

clue.text: Vehicle, large, appearing in fixed shade

indicators.note: the vehicle and size letter turn up within the fixed word

parts.note: set means fixed
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A large vehicle comes in a set colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red, a particular colour or hue.

clue.text: Excellent movement drawing in singular religious follower

indicators.note: the combined word draws the extra letter into itself, enclosing it

parts.note: ACE means excellent
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

explanation.surface: A fine gesture attracts a lone devotee of some faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is a person of a faith who practises severe self-denial, so a devout follower of a religion.

clue.text: Bitter: excellent, endlessly full-flavoured, about foremost of beers

parts.note: ACE means excellent

indicators.note: the shortened flavour word goes round the beer letter
endlessly means without an end, so the flavour word loses its final letter

parts.note: rich food is full of flavour

indicators.note: the foremost of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bitter ale is reviewed as excellent and full of flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' tempts as the beer, but it is the adjective; RICH loses H by 'endlessly' to give RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic means sharp and harsh, as in tone or taste, much like biting or sour.

clue.text: Rising charge brought in to supply pet essential

indicators.note: the reversed charge is placed inside the supplying word

parts.note: to cater is to supply food

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to tilt is to charge, as at windmills

explanation.surface: A rising charge is passed on to suppliers of pet necessities.
explanation.walkthrough: To tilt is to charge with a lance, as Don Quixote did at windmills; 'Rising' reads it upwards as TLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent granules for an indoor feline's tray are a necessity for a cat owner.

clue.text: Label majority of French game to get hot Mediterranean salad

parts.note: a tab is a label

indicators.note: most of the word, here all but its last letter

parts.note: boules is the French bowls game

explanation.surface: A label on a French game gets a hot salad dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This Lebanese dish of bulgur wheat, parsley and mint is eaten across the Levant.

clue.text: Laughter: difficult job suppressing this laughter initially

indicators.note: the job word holds down the initials inside it

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A tough task stifles initial giggles.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a type of merriment.

clue.text: Diversify, I say, coming in against a tax

parts.note: V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: the two short pieces come into the levy word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a rate is a local tax
EG, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Someone protesting a tax suggests spreading the burden more widely.
explanation.definitionFit: To variegate is to mark with varied colours, hence to make diverse or give variety.

clue.text: Very much split by a book ban

indicators.note: the phrase for excess is split apart with the short pieces dropped into it

parts.note: too means excessively, very much

explanation.surface: A book is banned for being far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a prohibition, social or religious, on some act or word.

clue.text: Poet to look good?

definitions.meaning: Edith, Osbert or Sacheverell, the literary English siblings of that surname
split 3,4, clothes that ... suit you and look good

explanation.surface: A poet aspires to appear attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edith of that name was a modernist English poet; a garment that sits well flatters the wearer.

clue.text: Be unwell in attack of ill-health leading to rescue

indicators.note: 'in' places the ailing word inside the attack word, within it

parts.note: a bout is a spell of illness, such as a bout of flu
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: Falling sick during a fit of illness leads to someone being saved.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailout is a financial rescue, as of a failing bank or firm.

clue.text: Painful time and tense when daughter leaves to tour university

indicators.note: the shortened word travels round the university letter, so it encloses it
the daughter letter departs from the gripping word

parts.note: a dramatic, tense moment

explanation.surface: A daughter leaving to go on a university tour makes for a tense, painful time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like grammar beside 'time' but means DRAMATIC; dropping D leaves RAMATIC, which goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traumatic is deeply distressing, causing emotional pain or shock.

clue.text: Outburst restrained by a father hard on a set of religious texts

indicators.note: the outburst is held within the father word

parts.note: POP is a name for father
a cry is an outburst
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A father suppresses an outburst over a hard sacred book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical books of doubtful authority, excluded from many canons of scripture.

clue.text: Extremism? It's in Italian city, and city's to dismiss it

indicators.note: the pronoun is in the city, placed inside its name

parts.note: Milan is a city in Italy
read as 'it is', so IT is the piece that goes inside

indicators.note: the city word dismisses, drops, the pronoun

parts.note: read as 'city is', the city word that does the dismissing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Extremism found in an Italian city, which the city wants to expel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dismiss' removes IT from CITY, leaving CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Militancy is aggressive, combative activism for a cause, an example of extremism, hence the query.

clue.text: Fabric lines appearing during day

indicators.note: the lines show up in the middle of the day's short form, inside it

parts.note: TUE is short for Tuesday
L is short for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Lines show up in a fabric during the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine silk or nylon netting used for veils and ballet skirts, a type of material.

clue.text: Boat stuck beside lake? That's a bad look

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: A boat stranded by a lake earns a dirty look.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl is an angry frowning expression, an unfriendly facial look.

clue.text: Are brought in lost, like sheep, often

indicators.note: the word is brought inside the lost word

parts.note: shed means cast off, lost

explanation.surface: Sheep often get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are regularly clipped of their fleece, which is what happens to them when shorn.

clue.text: Like a king or queen, adapting Roman style

indicators.note: adapting alters the letters of the city adjective into a new order

parts.note: chic means stylishness

explanation.surface: Royal grandeur achieved by adopting a Roman fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchic means relating to a monarch, a sovereign ruler, so royal.

clue.text: Grim carriage, with horse either side

indicators.note: the horse word is placed either side of the carriage, around it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A gloomy carriage, flanked by horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome, dwelling on death, hence grim.

clue.text: Individual dodging initial chaos, brought about one source of vengeance

indicators.note: the word avoids its first letter, losing it

parts.note: ONE is an individual

indicators.note: the chaos word is brought round the numeral

parts.note: a mess is chaos
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An individual escaping initial chaos brings on revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so an agent of righteous retribution.

clue.text: Series about historical king produces exasperation

indicators.note: the series word goes about, around, the royal letters

parts.note: a chain is a series
GR, Georgius Rex, stands for a former King George

explanation.surface: A series about a past monarch annoys viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is distress at being disappointed or humiliated, close to vexation.

clue.text: Quote to secure a high-class car turned unreliable

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is turned round to read backwards
the citing word holds the car pieces fast within it

parts.note: to cite is to quote
RR is Rolls-Royce, the classic upmarket car

explanation.surface: A quoted price for a luxury car turns out to be untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quote' looks like a price quote but is a verb; 'turned' reads the enclosure CITARRE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic is inconsistent and unpredictable, so not to be depended on.

clue.text: A skin blemish concealed by old woman's make-up

indicators.note: the blemish phrase is hidden within the mother word, enclosed by it

parts.note: MA is mother, one's old woman
a scar is a mark on the skin

explanation.surface: An elderly lady hides a skin mark with cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic for darkening the eyelashes, one kind of facial cosmetics.

clue.text: Man following dietary concerns up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: fats are what dieters worry over

explanation.surface: A man pursues his concerns about diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a verb here, to crew or operate.
explanation.definitionFit: To staff a desk or post is to provide people to operate it, to crew it.

clue.text: Tree, a polled tree

indicators.note: polled means beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: an elder is a shrub or small tree

explanation.surface: A tree described as a pollarded tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polled' suggests pollarding but here it removes the head letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a birch-family tree of damp ground.

clue.text: Northern city to continue splitting?

definitions.meaning: a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England
split 3,2, to ... is to keep on tearing

explanation.surface: A northern city will keep on dividing.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords anywhere in England north of the Midlands may be called northern.
explanation.definitionFit: This small cathedral city lies in North Yorkshire; going on ripping is continuing to tear.

clue.text: Second-rate, awfully nasty Left-wing revolutionary seen in Spectator

parts.note: B is a second-class grade, second-rate

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of the unpleasant word are badly mangled
revolutionary means the left-wing word turns right round

parts.note: RED means left-wing, socialist

explanation.surface: A political magazine is seen sneering at a mediocre, unpleasant radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges NASTY into YSTAN; 'revolutionary' turns RED into DER. The Spectator is a British political weekly, a deliberate red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander is an onlooker who watches without taking part, as a spectator does.

clue.text: A remedy that's failed? That's unfortunate

indicators.note: a failed remedy is one gone wrong, so its letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A cure didn't work: what a shame.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a mild expression of dismay or sympathy, like 'oh dear'.

clue.text: Small offence, carrying off last valuable plant

indicators.note: carrying off the final letter takes away the end of the offence word

parts.note: an affront is an insult, an offence

explanation.surface: A minor offence ends up removing the last precious plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus that yields saffron spice is famously costly, the priciest spice by weight.
